name: Print production and prepress
one_line: The controlled transition from designed artwork to a press-ready proof, production run and delivery record, where colour, imposition, approval and printer paperwork matter more than the artwork medium.

deterministic: A labelled proof-to-press packet containing a proof approval, press specification or imposition sheet, and a printer job reference is a print-production workflow signal.
A printer or prepress report that names an artwork file, colour process, trim/bleed, stock, plates or press run is production evidence when paired with the referenced artwork or job record.
A delivery manifest or packing record that names the printed quantity, recipient and the same printer job reference can close the workflow when it is paired with proof or production evidence.
A mixed archive whose manifest contains artwork, preflight output, proof, approval, press specification and delivery records under one job reference is a bounded print-production packet.
needs_llm: deciding whether an item labelled final or approved is a customer-approved proof, an internal design export, or a legal/commercial approval
deciding whether a printer name is the production vendor, a paper or ink supplier, a client, or merely a logo appearing in a reference document
joining a press report, email and exported PDF when names differ but the job identity is expressed in prose or a scanned purchase-order attachment
separating a delivered printed object record from a design portfolio image or photographed finished work
never_alone: a .pdf, .ps, .eps, .ai, .indd, .tif or .zip extension; file type is routing evidence only
CMYK, spot colour, ICC profile, bleed, trim, crop marks, overprint, imposition or embedded-font metadata without a job or proof context
the words print, press, proof, final, approved, plate, run or delivered in a filename alone
a printer, paper mill, courier or client name without a labelled role and linked production evidence
a quantity, date, purchase-order number or invoice alone; these may belong to finance, procurement or logistics
a flat photograph or scan of a printed poster, book or package without prepress or production-record evidence
a shared folder, bounded download session, matching stem or archive co-occurrence alone
a colour swatch, registration mark or page-box observation alone

grouping_reasons: one print job from supplied artwork through preflight, proof, approval, press record and delivery
one proof round and the exact comments or approval that answer it
one printer job reference across production paperwork and its named artwork exports
one delivered edition or batch when quantity, recipient and production record agree
do not copy a project, client, vendor or approval fact from a neighbouring file merely because it shares a filename stem

template.why: The creative schema currently declares no fields, so no serializable folder dimensions are legal. Print production remains a distinct activation situation through its proof→press→run→delivery evidence; medium, colour process, vendor, quantity and format are workflow observations or values, not new field keys. It is not time-first because one job contains several clocks (artwork, proof, approval, press and delivery).

collides_with.signal: A press-ready export, proof or artwork PDF may be the ordinary design-making record. Print production requires linked proof, press, run or delivery evidence; a format or CMYK property alone stays with graphic design or the creative default.

Printer quotes, supplier onboarding and invoices may concern the vendor relationship rather than a specific creative job. Vendor management owns the counterparty administration; this template owns job-specific proof-to-run evidence.
A press run record resembles a manufacturing batch record. Print production requires artwork/proof context and a print job; generic shop-floor production records belong to manufacturing.
Packing lists, tracking and delivery manifests can be logistics records. They enter this workflow only when tied to the print job's production packet; transport-only evidence belongs to shipment.

falls_through_to.why: A lone proof, report or manifest without a coherent job neighbourhood remains an independent record.
Conflicting proof, approval or delivery evidence requires review rather than an automatic production grouping.
A photograph or scan of a printed object without production evidence is an isolated image.
A printer invoice or courier confirmation without artwork and production linkage is a transactional record.

sensitivity_why: Unreleased artwork, client approvals, quantities, addresses, supplier pricing and delivery details may be sensitive. The placeholder schema has no field rows, so this records protection posture without inventing handling classes or destination fields.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH: whether a future creative schema should adopt project, stage, artifact_type and client (or a dedicated production-job handle). Until that decision, print production remains a workflow template with no serialized dimensions; do not promote vendor, quantity, colour process or format into fields.
